title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching and quant profiles; unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce autotuned defaults for batching/caching windows and quantization profile selection. Add unit-economics CLI for recommending profiles and rollout behind feature flag. Backwards compatible; safe rollout via feature flag and gradual percentage-based canary.
description:
Context: Customers running high-throughput inference want predictable unit economics without heavy manual tuning. This PR introduces an autotune path that sets conservative defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching and adds a workload-aware quantization profile selector. It also ships a lightweight unit-econ CLI that recommends batching/caching/quant profiles for a given request distribution.

Summary of changes: consolidated autotune algorithm (optimize/autotune.py), new default parameters in runtime batching/cache, quant_profiles.yaml with automated scoring heuristics, unit-econ CLI and integration tests, docs and rollout/feature flagging.

Why this change: Repeated customer requests and internal benchmarks showed that a small number of sensible defaults + an automated recommendation tool reduces per-token cost by ~15-25% on typical production workloads while keeping p99 latency within SLOs. This reduces time-to-deploy and reduces manual experimentation.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc / Linear ENG-3121 linked - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks (see performance_results) - [x] Feature flag gating + rollout plan - [x] Docs updated (cost-optimization guide)

Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag cost_autotune_v1=false by default. Enable canary for 5% of traffic, monitor token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, fallback to previous behavior on regressions. After 2 weeks of stable metrics, increase to 25% then full rollout.

Notes: The description below includes high-level commit summaries and file changes. For implementation details see changed_files and commits fields.

feat(quant): add quant_profiles.yaml and heuristic selector

chore(docs): add cost-optimization guide and rollout notes
review_comments: Miguel Torres: High level this looks great - the heuristic for choosing quant profiles needs one more safety check to avoid 8-bit for low-memory GPUs. Can you add a guard?
Asha Patel: Added a GPU-capability guard in autotune.py and updated quant_profiles.yaml to include min_hw_capability. Also added a unit test covering the guard.
Evelyn Chen: CI initially failed on integration perf test (timeout). Is this flaky or a regression?
Asha Patel: It was a flaky test due to timing assumptions. I stabilized the test by mocking the scheduler clock and re-ran CI. All tests passed on re-run.
Ravi Krishnan: Suggest we expose the recommendation output in the Console as an opt-in report. We can follow up in a separate PR. Approved once CI green.
Miguel Torres: Approving - verified local benchmark numbers and code changes.

merge_commit_message:
squash: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching and quant profiles; add unit-econ tooling

Linked: ENG-3121, PM-148
performance_results: Workload A (conversational customer support): token-cost reduction ~18% (baseline: $0.00345/token -> new: $0.00283/token), median latency p50 stable (120ms -> 125ms), p99 +4% (450ms -> 468ms) within SLO
Workload B (short prompts, high QPS): token-cost reduction ~23% due to improved batching (baseline: $0.00110/token -> new: $0.00085/token), p50 improved slightly (40ms -> 36ms), p99 unchanged
Safe-mode fallback tested: when quant selector recommends aggressive profile and p99 regresses >10% the runtime falls back to conservative profile automatically.
unit_econ_tooling_notes: The unit-econ CLI simulates request distributions using a small trace sample (CSV) and outputs ranked recommendations for batching window, prefix/KV cache TTL, and quant profile. Integration test verifies CLI suggestions applied to a local runtime instance reduce simulated cost by >10% for typical traces.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for autotune scoring, quant selection guards, and mocked perf harness for deterministic results. Integration tests exercise end-to-end recommendation and runtime application behind feature flag.
docs_notes: redwood/docs/cost-optimization.md contains user-facing guidance, examples of using the unit-econ CLI, interpreting recommendations, and rollout checklist. Also linked from Console docs.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive quantization and batching could increase tail latency for some customers. Mitigation: feature flag, canary rollout, automated regression detection (alerts in redwood/observability/alerts), and automatic fallback to conservative profiles.
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag cost_autotune_v1=false by default. Ops run canary as documented in cost-optimization guide. Expect telemetry to show unit-econ metrics under redwood.metrics.unit_econ.* tag.
human_readable_summary: Adds autotune defaults and a workload-aware quantization selector to reduce per-token unit cost. Ships a unit-economics CLI that recommends config changes based on trace samples. Feature-flagged rollout and automated safeguards included.
